text: ServiceNow provides a real archiving and rotation capability: a scheduled job that moves records matching defined criteria, typically closed more than a few years ago, out of the live, active table and into a separate archive table, or deletes them outright per a defined retention rule. The record isn't gone from the organization's history — it's moved out of the table every live query, list view, and report has to search through.

This connects directly to course 12's indexing and query-performance content. An index helps a query find the right rows faster within a table of a given size, but a smaller active table is faster to query and index regardless of how good the indexing is — fewer rows means a smaller index to traverse and a tighter working set. Good indexing and a disciplined archiving policy aren't competing strategies. They're the same goal, query performance, attacked from two different angles.

Here's the part that isn't purely technical. Once a record is archived, it becomes less immediately accessible to end users and reports — pulling it back usually requires knowing it's archived and going to look for it. So an architect has to weigh query performance on the active table against a genuine business or compliance need to keep some historical data readily accessible, like an active legal hold or an ongoing audit.

There's no formula that resolves this automatically. A three-year retention window might be exactly right for one table and badly wrong for another, depending on what that business actually does with its old data. A sound policy defines its criteria precisely, confirms them against any real compliance requirement first, decides deliberately between archiving and outright deletion, and gets revisited periodically as requirements change.

Archiving keeps the active table's query performance healthy as data accumulates over years of production use, but it's a judgment call balanced against real business need, not a purely technical setting. Next up: the same kind of long-term discipline, applied to CSDM governance across an entire enterprise.
